leagues.name: ICC events
notes: The ICC is a governing body, not a league; its commercial partners cover its major events rather than team shirts. Modelled like FIFA: one partner list covering the four senior events in the 2026-27 window.

Premier Partners (top tier): Emirates, Aramco, DP World, Hyundai. Global Partners: Coca-Cola, Budweiser (AB InBev), Google, Sobha Realty, Rexona (Unilever), Marriott Bonvoy. Official supporter: Royal Stag (per https://www.icc-cricket.com/about/partners, fetched 2026-09-25).

Rosters differ slightly per event: the Women's T20 World Cup 2026 footer showed Rexona but not Sobha Realty; the men's-event footers show Sobha Realty. Rexona rides the Unilever women's-cricket deal (women's events only), Sobha Realty is a men's-events-only Global Partner.
ICC's Cricket 4 Good sits in the 'official supporters' footer block but is the ICC's own social-responsibility programme, not a sponsor.

Side note, not researched as a target: the UAE's ILT20 (Emirates Cricket Board) has DP World as title sponsor; franchise owners per Wikipedia (lead only): Reliance, Adani, GMR, Knight Riders, Lancer Capital, Capri Global.

why.text: Dubai is part of the United Arab Emirates, where criticising the government can land you in prison. In 2024, 43 activists got life sentences in a single mass trial. Putting Emirates on a famous shirt makes the country look good to millions of fans while that goes on. That's called sportswashing.
why.messageLine: In 2024, 43 activists in the UAE got life sentences in one mass trial.

claims.text: DP World Limited's audited FY2025 financial statements state that Port & Free Zone World FZE ('PFZW'), a wholly owned subsidiary of Dubai World Corporation, holds 100% of the company's issued and outstanding share capital, and that the Government of Dubai is the ultimate owner of the group.

source.name: DP World Annual Report 2025 (consolidated financial statements), DP World Limited, DIFC, year ended 31 December 2025

claims.text: Two ICC Premier Partners sit at the top of chains that end with the Government of Dubai (Emirates, via the Dubai government's investment arm; DP World, whose ultimate owner the company states is the Government of Dubai). Human Rights Watch documented that in 2024 a UAE court sentenced 43 Emirati activists and dissidents to life imprisonment after a mass trial, and that the Federal Supreme Court upheld the convictions in March 2025.

source.name: Human Rights Watch: UAE: 43 Life Sentences in 'Flagrant Injustice' (mass trial) and follow-up on upheld convictions

proposedRatings.reasoning: Already rated serious in the corpus and the rating carries over unchanged: Aramco is majority-owned (81.48%) by the Government of Saudi Arabia with a further 16% held by the state's PIF, and it is the Saudi state's economic engine. It is a Premier Partner of every ICC event in the window through the end of 2027, with its brand on Player of the Tournament and Power Rating assets, so the same state link applies across all four target events.

Already rated serious: Emirates is owned by the Government of Dubai through Investment Corporation of Dubai, and the UAE mass-trial claims (43 life sentences in 2024, upheld in 2025) attach to that owner chain. As an ICC Premier Partner to 2031 with naming rights over the match officials, the sportswashing logic is the same as on a club shirt.

New sponsor, but the ownership chain is fully documented to the top: DP World Limited's FY2025 audited statements name Port & Free Zone World FZE (100% shareholder) under Dubai World Corporation, and state that the Government of Dubai is the ultimate owner. That makes DP World the third Gulf state-owned company in the ICC's top tier, exactly the pattern the target flags. Proposing the same serious tier as Emirates, resting on the same UAE mass-trial claims plus the ownership claim.

Already rated concern: the parent's register carries genuine but minority state money (Korean National Pension Service 7.76%, GIC 3.55%) while control sits with the Chung family via a circular chaebol ring - the rubric's partial state stake, not state control. Hyundai became an ICC Premier Partner in December 2025, so the existing rating now applies to a fourth sport.

unsourced: No contract values for any ICC partnership are public in ICC's own releases; trade-press figures (SportBusiness, SportsPro, ESPNcricinfo) were not verifiable this pass because those publishers block fetching - all deals are filed with value: null.
DP World deal end date: neither the June 2023 announcement nor the May 2024 elevation to Premier Partner states a term ('long-term' only).
Hyundai deal end date: the December 2025 announcement says 'multi-year' only.
Sobha Realty deal end date: the February 2025 announcement states no term.
Google deal end date: the August 2025 women's-cricket partnership announcement states no term; the February 2026 Gemini/Pixel Men's T20 World Cup activation is also undated in duration.
Aramco original partnership start: the May 2024 extension references a successful 'initial 18-month term', implying a late-2022 start, but the original announcement was not located this pass.

Women's T20 World Cup 2026 footer shows Rexona (Unilever) among Global Partners but not Sobha Realty; men's-event footers show Sobha Realty. The /about/partners page (fetched 2026-09-25) lists both. Whether this is a per-event rights split (women's vs men's events) or a page-staleness issue is unresolved - the underlying Unilever deal is women's-cricket-only and Sobha Realty is men's-events-only, which is consistent with both observations.
Emirates' earlier ICC contract terms (the deal in force before the 2024 extension) are not stated; the May 2024 release says only that the partnership is 'already in its third decade'.
AB InBev deal value and whether the partnership ends exactly at end-2027 or extends beyond: the December 2025 announcement covers events 'through 2027' only.

ILT20 (side note, out of scope): DP World title sponsorship and franchise ownership (Reliance, Adani, GMR, Knight Riders, Lancer Capital, Capri Global) are known only from Wikipedia, used as a lead, never cited as a source.

Broadcast partners (Star Sports, Disney+ Hotstar, Sky Sports, SuperSport, Willow, Prime Video, CricLife, Myco, PTV Sports, ESPN, Sky NZ, TSM, Dialog, ICC TV) appear in the partners-page footer above the labelled tiers; their deal terms and whether they count as sponsors for this project are unresolved. Shapes event-host / org-partner facts (award naming, umpire-kit branding, perimeter/broadcast branding, per-event host entities) do not fit the kits/deals schema and are recorded here rather than forced in.

Royal Stag's owner: the ICC release quotes Pernod Ricard India's CMO, strongly indicating the brand belongs to Pernod Ricard, but a primary document confirming the ownership chain (Seagram's Royal Stag under Pernod Ricard India) was not opened this pass, so ownerId is left null.
